name: Partial incision double eyelid

lead: Partial-incision double-eyelid surgery creates a supratarsal fold in the upper eyelid through a few short incisions instead of one long one. The result is a defined crease that changes how the eye looks and opens.

Surgeons describe it as combining benefits of the full-incision and non-incision methods, with a predictable and durable crease [1][2]. Published series report techniques for natural-looking, stable folds [3][4].

paras: A surgeon designs the crease with the patient sitting upright and makes small incisions along it. Sutures fix skin to the levator aponeurosis, and fat or muscle may be removed in some variations. Recovery involves swelling and later suture removal.

Described concerns include unstable or shallow creases and a depressed firm crease when pretarsal muscle is removed, which newer techniques aim to avoid [2]. Wikipedia notes swelling and bruising are common after eyelid surgery and usually settle over weeks [5].

angle.text: The operation creates a visible upper-eyelid crease. Some versions also address mild ptosis, which can make the eyes look more open [4].

lead: Partial-incision double-eyelid blepharoplasty creates an upper-eyelid crease (supratarsal fold) through several small incisions rather than a full-length cut. It is a popular aesthetic operation in East Asia [1][2].

One 2014 study described a three-mini-incision technique with 3-4 mm cuts that removes pretarsal muscle and excess fat and joins levator aponeurosis to skin for a stable, natural-looking fold [3]. A 2023 series of 132 Chinese patients described a modified method that preserves the orbicularis muscle to give a more dynamic, durable crease with a less visible scar and shorter recovery [1].
Variants include a combined partial- and minimal-incision method [2] and a three-point vertical mattress suture for mild ptosis alongside crease creation in 57 patients [4].

paras: The method sits between full-incision and non-incision approaches, offering predictability and durability with minimal scars [2].

The three-mini-incision approach removes a strip of pretarsal orbicularis and excess fat and creates a firm connection with the levator aponeurosis [3]. Orbicularis-preserving versions aim to avoid the depressed, firm crease seen with muscle resection [1]. Planning is done with the patient upright, with partial incisions between the medial limbus and mid-pupillary line and a minimal incision near the lateral limbus in one variation [2].
Eyelid surgery commonly causes swelling and bruising that resolve over weeks; cold compresses and head elevation are often recommended [5].

Studies are mostly surgical case series: a 3-mini-incision clinical study [3], 132 patients in a retrospective modified technique [1], a combined partial and minimal incision series [2], and 57 patients with mild ptosis correction [4]. They report stable, natural-looking creases from the authors' own techniques.
